blog_summary: Adrian Colyer highlights Google's WSMeter as a novel methodology for evaluating the performance of warehouse-scale computers (WSCs) in live production environments. The key challenge WSMeter addresses is the impracticality of load-testing benchmarks for WSCs, which run thousands of diverse jobs. WSMeter proposes a quota-weighted performance metric that aggregates individual job performance, weighted by CPU quota, to produce a single WSC-wide performance number. The approach focuses on a subset of heavyweight, common jobs (10-20%) to reduce computational overhead while maintaining accuracy. Colyer notes that this method inherently prioritizes improvements for large jobs, potentially at the expense of tail performance, but argues it works well for Google's workload characteristics. The paper also introduces a statistical model using t-distributions and normal approximations to handle performance variability across job instances, with a SAT solver optimizing sample sizes for accuracy and cost.
paper_title: WSMeter: A performance evaluation methodology for Google’s production warehouse-scale computers
